# survey-skill

An agent skill for Qualtrics® `.qsf` survey files, focused on the quirks:
what real exports contain, what breaks silently, how SSO behaves. It
assumes a frontier model that already knows the QSF basics.

New to this? Start with the plain-language guide in
[`instructions/`](instructions/guide.md): what the sample
surveys do, how to import them and how to switch on sign-in. Common questions
are answered in the [FAQ](instructions/FAQ.md). Indicative screenshots in [`screenshots/`](screenshots/).

## Quick start
1. Use or upload the distribution file [dist/survey-skill-bundle.txt](dist/survey-skill-bundle.txt) to your AI web service or harness and describe what survey you want
2. Import the survey into Qualtrics
3. If SSO is needed, reselect the SSO type to Shibboleth as described in [FAQ](instructions/FAQ.md#Shibboleth)

## Layout

```
Makefile                       shortcuts: make validate | test | bundle | clean
skills/survey-qsf/
  SKILL.md                     the skill: modes, export quirks, recompute list, SSO essentials
  references/sso.md            authenticator shape, placement, failure modes, diagnosis
  references/feature-shapes.md copy-ready JSON for branches, embedded data, ranking, validation, JS/CSS
  scripts/validate_qsf.py      structural validator (stdlib); --fresh for generated files
  samples/                     three anonymized sample surveys, each with an SSO authenticator
tests/test_validate_qsf.py     validator + sample tests
scripts/
  make_bundle.sh              one-file bundle of all docs + validator + samples (for AI web uploads)
instructions/                  plain-language guide: import the samples, set up sign-in
  guide.md                     the guide
  FAQ.md                       common questions
screenshots/                   screenshots of the steps in the guide
```

## Samples

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `session-availability-sso.qsf` | Sign in, then mark each of 8 one-hour slots as no / remote / on site / either |
| `ranked-preferences-sso.qsf` | Sign in, opt in, pick exactly 3 of 10 options, drag them into rank order, comment |
| `event-attendance-sso.qsf` | Sign up via SSO or manually, RSVP yes / no, add the event to a calendar (Google/Outlook links, `.ics` download) |

All three show a Qualtrics page before the authenticator and carry placeholder
SSO values (`ASC_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`, key `XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX`). After import
(new project → Survey → *Import a QSF file*), open Survey flow, select your
brand's SSO connection in the authenticator, publish, and test on the
anonymous link (SSO is unreliable in preview). If the link says "Error
while determining which SSO connection to use", the selection was not
stored: switch SSO Type to another value, save, switch back, re-select
the connection, save and publish.

## Install the skill

Clone the repo, then copy or symlink `skills/survey-qsf/` into your agent's
skills folder, e.g. for [pi](https://pi.dev/):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/all-hands/survey-skill.git
cd survey-skill
ln -s "$PWD/skills/survey-qsf" ~/.pi/agent/skills/survey-qsf
```

## Validate and test

```sh
python3 skills/survey-qsf/scripts/validate_qsf.py skills/survey-qsf/samples/*.qsf --fresh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

With `make`: `make validate`, `make test`, `make bundle` (one-file bundle for
AI services that accept a single upload), `make clean` — wrappers for the
commands above.

One test scans every tracked text file for the words in
`tests/forbidden_terms.txt` (one regex per line, git-ignored, so it is not
in a fresh clone). Without that file the test fails. To run the tests
without it, set `SURVEY_SKILL_NO_TERMS=1`. Images are not scanned: check
screenshots by eye.

## Real exports are secrets

A `.qsf` exported from a survey with an SSO authenticator embeds the SSO
connection's token key. Keep real exports out of this repo: `exports/` and
`*.private.qsf` are git-ignored for that.

## Made with AI

The initial skill, validator, tests, sample surveys and guide in this repo were
created with open-weight AI models. Final polishing was made with a mix of open- and closed-weight models.

# Ready-made Qualtrics surveys with sign-in: a plain guide

## In short

**What it is.** Three example surveys you can load into Qualtrics, plus
written guidance for the colleague or AI assistant who builds surveys
for you.

**Who it is for.** Anyone who runs surveys in Qualtrics through the web
page and wants to know who answered, without asking participants to type their
name.

**What you get.** Each example asks participants to sign in with their work
account first. Their name, email and ID then land in your results by
themselves. No typing, no typos.

No technical knowledge needed. A few words come back often:

- **QSF file**: one file that holds a whole Qualtrics survey. You load it
  into Qualtrics and get a ready-made survey.
- **SSO** (single sign-on): participants log in with the same work account they
  use for email. Your organisation then tells Qualtrics who they are.
- **Survey flow**: the Qualtrics screen that shows the order of the
  survey's parts and the rules between them
  ([Qualtrics guide](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/survey-flow-overview/)).
- **Authenticator**: a step in the survey flow that asks participants to sign
  in before they see what comes after it
  ([Qualtrics guide](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/authenticator-overview/)).
- **Embedded data**: extra columns Qualtrics fills in by itself, for
  example the name it got from the sign-in
  ([Qualtrics guide](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/standard-elements/embedded-data/)).

The whole journey looks like this:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Sample .qsf file"] --> B["Import into Qualtrics"]
    B --> C["Survey flow: pick your SSO connection"]
    C --> D["Publish"]
    D --> E["Participant opens the link"]
    E --> F["Signs in with work account"]
    F --> G["Answers the questions"]
    G --> H["Results: name, email, ID and answers per row"]
```

Stuck, or a colleague can't sign in? Common questions are answered in
the [FAQ](FAQ.md).

## The three example surveys

All three start with a normal Qualtrics page that says what the survey
is about. Only then does the participant sign in. After sign-in they see a
small card: "Is this you? Your answers are linked to" with their name
and email.

### 1. Session availability

For planning: which slots can participants join, and how?

What the participant sees:

1. A welcome page: "Pick your slots". It says they will sign in first,
   and that all times are UTC.
2. The sign-in page of their organisation.
3. One page with the details card, then a grid. Each row is one of 8
   one-hour slots over three days. For each row they choose: no,
   remote, on site, or either. Every row needs an answer. Below
   is an optional comment box.
4. The thank-you page.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W["Page 1: welcome"] --> S["Sign in with work account"]
    S -->|login works| P["Page 2: details card, availability grid, comment"]
    S -->|login fails| X["Thank-you page, empty response saved"]
    P --> T["Thank-you page"]
```

What you get in the results: FirstName, LastName, Email and UserID from
the sign-in. Then one answer per slot, coded 1 to 4: 1 no,
2 remote, 3 on site, 4 either. Then the comment.

### 2. Ranked preferences

For choosing: participants pick their top 3 out of 10 options and put them in
order. The sample options are made up, such as "Internal
knowledge base" or "Accessibility audit". You replace them with your own.

What the participant sees:

1. A welcome page. It says they will sign in, pick 3 of 10 projects and
   order them, best first.
2. The sign-in page.
3. The details card and one question: "Submit your picks now?" Yes or
   not now.
4. If **yes**: a page with 10 options in two columns. They must pick
   exactly 3. After the third, the other boxes switch off.
5. A page where they drag their 3 picks into order, first choice on top.
   They must move at least one item, even if they like the order shown.
6. An optional comment page, then the thank-you page.

If **not now**: a short "No problem" page, then the thank-you page.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    W["Page 1: welcome"] --> S["Sign in with work account"]
    S -->|login fails| X["Thank-you page, empty response saved"]
    S -->|login works| I["Page 2: details card, submit picks now?"]
    I -->|Yes| C["Page 3: choose exactly 3 of 10"]
    C --> R["Page 4: drag the 3 into order"]
    R --> M["Page 5: optional comment"]
    M --> T["Thank-you page"]
    I -->|Not now| N["Page 3: no problem"]
    N --> T
```

What you get: FirstName, LastName, Email, UserID. A column
**OptIn** with yes or no. Which 3 options were picked, and the
rank given to each. Then the comment.

### 3. Event attendance

For events: will participants come? This one also lets in participants who have no
work account.

What the participant sees:

1. A page with the event details (a sample lunch talk: date, time, room)
   and one question: "How do you want to sign up?" Sign in with my work
   account, or sign up without an account.
2. Sign-in route: the sign-in page, then a page with the details card.
   Other route: the same page, but with required boxes for first name,
   last name and a valid email instead of the card.
3. On that page, for both: "Can you make it?" (Yes / No), an optional
   notes box, and buttons to add the event to a calendar: Google
   Calendar, Outlook, or a calendar file for other apps.
4. They press "Done" and see the thank-you page.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    E["Page 1: event details, how to sign up?"] -->|Sign in| S["Sign in with work account"]
    E -->|Without an account| F2["Page 2: type name and email, RSVP, notes, calendar"]
    S -->|login works| F1["Page 2: details card, RSVP, notes, calendar"]
    S -->|login fails| X["Thank-you page, empty response saved"]
    F1 --> A{"Can you make it?"}
    F2 --> A
    A -->|Yes| Y["Saved: RsvpStatus = yes"]
    A -->|No| Z["Saved: RsvpStatus = no"]
    Y --> T["Thank-you page"]
    Z --> T
```

The two "Saved" steps happen behind the scenes. The participant does not
see them.

What you get: FirstName, LastName and Email for everyone. Typed answers
are copied into the same columns, so all rows look alike. UserID is
filled only for participants who signed in. A column **LoginMethod** says SSO or Manual. A
column **RsvpStatus** says yes or no. The RSVP question itself is coded
1 for yes, 0 for no. Typed email
addresses are less reliable; expect some to bounce.

## Try a sample yourself

1. Download one of the three files from the project's
   `skills/survey-qsf/samples` folder:
   `session-availability-sso.qsf`, `ranked-preferences-sso.qsf` or
   `event-attendance-sso.qsf`. Save it; no need to open it.
2. In Qualtrics, create a new project, choose **Survey**, and pick
   **Import a QSF file**. Select the file you saved
   ([how importing works](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-tools/import-and-export-surveys/)).
3. Open **Survey flow**.
4. Click the authenticator step. Choose your organisation's SSO
   connection from the list. The file only holds a placeholder (a row of
   X's), so this step is a must. If no connection is listed, ask your
   Qualtrics brand administrator (the person who manages your
   organisation's Qualtrics account). They switch it on as described in
   [Configuring Organization SSO Settings](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/sp-administration/brand-customization-services/sso/configuring-organization-sso-settings/). The same applies if you later move
   the survey to another Qualtrics account: choose the connection again.
5. Publish the survey.
6. Take the
   [anonymous link](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/distributions-module/web-distribution/anonymous-link/).
   Open it in a normal browser window and go through the survey as a
   participant would. Do not test with preview: sign-in through preview is
   unreliable, as
   [Qualtrics itself warns](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/sso-authenticator/).
7. Look at your test response in the results. Your name and email should
   be there.

**If the link shows "Error while determining which SSO connection to use
for this survey".** It may be that the SSO connection is not registered
yet: the editor shows your connection, but the survey did not store it.
The number in brackets after the message is only a report reference. Fix:

1. Open **Survey flow** and click the authenticator step.
2. In the **SSO Type** dropdown, select another method. Save the flow.
   If saving does not stick, publish and then unpublish the survey.
3. Switch **SSO Type** back to your original type and select your
   connection again.
4. Save the flow and publish again. If saving does not stick, publish
   once more.
5. Test again with the anonymous link, in a new normal browser window.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    E["Link shows: Error while determining which SSO connection"] --> O["Survey flow: open the authenticator"]
    O --> A["SSO Type: select another method, save"]
    A --> B["SSO Type: back to your type, select connection"]
    B --> C["Save and publish"]
    C --> T["Test with a fresh anonymous link"]
    T -->|still an error| A
```

Then change the texts, dates and options to your own.

Note: the files pass every check in the project, but have not been
tried in every Qualtrics account. Small things may differ after import.
For example, the error text shown when a participant picks the wrong number of
options may need to be set again in the editor.

## Why sign in first

- Nobody types their name, so there are no typos and no nicknames.
- You know who answered: each row carries the participant's ID.
- The details card lets participants see that the survey knows who they are.

Two practical warnings:

- **A failed sign-in skips the survey.** If a participant cannot sign in,
  Qualtrics sends them past all the questions to the thank-you page. They
  will say "the survey ended at once". Qualtrics still saves an almost
  empty response
  ([Qualtrics on failed authentication](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/authenticator-overview/)).
  Before you count results, remove rows without an email or ID.
- **Tell participants to use a normal browser.** Sign-in can fail when the link
  is opened inside the Teams or Outlook app, or in a private window.
  Strict privacy settings and ad blockers can also get in the way. Ask
  participants to copy the link into a normal browser window.

Also good to know:

- Participants can fill in the survey more than once. Each time is a new row.
  Keep the last row per UserID.
- If the details card shows an empty name, the participant's account did not
  pass it on. The team that runs your organisation's login can fix that.
- The page before the sign-in is on purpose: going straight to sign-in
  is known to fail for some participants.

## Email participants a copy of their answers

Qualtrics can email each participant their own answers as soon as they
finish. You set this up once per survey as a **workflow**: an automatic
"when this happens, do that" rule
([Qualtrics guide](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/actions-module/email-task/)).

The samples already keep each participant's email address in a column
called **Email**. It comes from the sign-in, or from what they typed in
the event sample. The workflow sends to that column.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R["Participant finishes the survey"] --> W["Workflow starts"]
    W --> C{"Email filled in?"}
    C -->|yes| M["Email: thank-you plus their answers"]
    C -->|no| S["Nothing sent"]
    M --> I["Participant's inbox"]
```

1. Open the survey and go to the **Workflows** tab. Click **Create a
   workflow**, then **Started when an event is received**.
2. Choose the **Survey response** event, for new responses only (not
   updated or deleted ones).
3. Click **+**, then **Add a condition**: Embedded data **Email** is not
   empty. That skips rows without an address. In the event sample you
   can add a second condition, for example only participants who said
   yes.
4. Click **+**, then **Add a task**, and choose **Email**.
5. Fill in the email:
   - **To**: click the piped text button, choose **Embedded Data Field**
     and type `Email`. It shows up as `${e://Field/Email}`.
   - **From Name**: your name or your team's. Leave the **From Address**
     as it is, unless your organisation has set up its own.
   - **Reply-To**: an address where you actually read replies.
   - **Subject**: for example "Your answers: slot availability".
   - **Message**: a short thank-you. Piped text can add their first name
     (`${e://Field/FirstName}`) or a single answer.
   - Tick **Include Response Report** to add all their answers. In its
     options, set **Expiration** to a short period, such as 7 days: it
     controls how long the link and the PDF keep working. Qualtrics
     warns when you choose Never; don't, because the answers are
     personal. Set the embedded data to **None** or only the survey
     flow's fields, so internal columns stay out of the email.
6. Save the task, check that the workflow is switched on, and publish
   the survey.
7. Test with the anonymous link and your own account, then check your
   inbox and spam folder. Test and preview responses send real emails
   too, so only test with your own address.

Good to know:

- Only finished responses send an email. A participant who stops
  halfway gets nothing.
- Typed addresses in the event sample can be wrong, and those emails
  bounce.
- Nothing arrives? See
  [the FAQ on emails after a response](FAQ.md#emails-after-a-response).

## Further reading

The [FAQ](FAQ.md) answers common questions: sign-in
problems, ranking and validation, emails after a response, themes.

All from the official Qualtrics support site:

- [Survey Flow Overview](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/survey-flow-overview/): the screen where you set the SSO connection.
- [Authenticator Overview](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/authenticator-overview/): where to place it, retakes, what happens when sign-in fails.
- [SSO Authenticator](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/sso-authenticator/): SSO types, the preview warning, error codes.
- [Configuring Organization SSO Settings](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/sp-administration/brand-customization-services/sso/configuring-organization-sso-settings/): for your brand administrator.
- [Embedded Data](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/standard-elements/embedded-data/): the extra columns filled by sign-in.
- [Import and Export Surveys](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-tools/import-and-export-surveys/): loading a `.qsf` file.
- [Anonymous Link](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/distributions-module/web-distribution/anonymous-link/): the link you send and test with.
- [Email Task](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/actions-module/email-task/): the email step in a workflow, including the response report.
- [Survey Theming](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/look-feel/applying-survey-themes/): change the look, logo and colours after import.

## For the technical colleague or AI assistant

You can stop reading here. An AI agent is an AI assistant that can read
and write files; a skill is a set of written instructions it reads before
a specific job. This project holds one skill for `.qsf` files (JSON
text): what real exports contain, what breaks silently on import, how the
SSO authenticator behaves, plus copy-ready pieces for branches, embedded
data, ranking and validation. A validator (a small program that checks a
file's structure) and 40 automated tests come with it. All three samples
pass, with one warning each: the SSO placeholder. Branch coverage is not
checked; that stays a human job. A real export with sign-in contains the
SSO connection's secret key: treat it like a password.

```sh
python3 skills/survey-qsf/scripts/validate_qsf.py skills/survey-qsf/samples/*.qsf --fresh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Drop `--fresh` when checking a real export instead of a generated file.

===============================================================================
FILE: instructions/FAQ.md

# Frequently asked questions

Common questions about surveys with sign-in (SSO). For the step-by-step
guide, see [the plain guide](guide.md).

Menu names in Qualtrics differ a little between accounts and change over
time. If a step doesn't match what you see, search the
[Qualtrics support site](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/) for the
setting's name.

## Sign-in (SSO)

### Sign-in works for me but not for a participant. What's wrong?

If the survey works for you, the setup is usually fine. Check these, in
this order:

1. **Preview link.** Did they open a preview link? Sign-in through
   preview is unreliable. Send them the anonymous link.
2. **Browser.** Links opened inside the Teams or Outlook app, private
   windows, strict privacy settings and ad blockers can break the
   sign-in. Ask them to paste the link into a normal browser window.
3. **Account type.** Guest or some staff accounts may not pass their
   name and email to Qualtrics. Only the team that runs your
   organisation's login can fix that.

A failed sign-in sends participants straight to the end of the survey, so they
will say "it ended at once". Qualtrics still saves an almost empty
response. Remove rows without an email or ID before you count results.

### Where does Qualtrics say preview doesn't work with SSO?

On the
[SSO Authenticator](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/sso-authenticator/)
support page, which warns that this SSO type "may not function properly
with Preview Survey" and suggests testing with the anonymous link.

### Could bot detection (reCAPTCHA) be blocking participants?

Unlikely. Qualtrics' support pages describe bot detection as adding a
score to each response; it doesn't stop any participant taking the survey. To
switch it off anyway: **Survey options › Security › Bot detection**,
then **Publish**. The live link keeps the old setting until you publish.

### After importing a sample, the link says "Error while determining which SSO connection to use". How do I fix it? ([Shibboleth](#Shibboleth))

The sample file only holds a placeholder connection, and the editor can
show your connection without actually saving it. This fix worked:

1. In **Survey flow**, open the authenticator.
2. Change **SSO Type** to another method and save. If saving doesn't
   stick, publish and then unpublish.
3. Switch **SSO Type** back and select your connection again.
4. Save and publish. If saving doesn't stick, publish once more.
5. Test with a fresh anonymous link in a normal browser window.

The number in brackets after the message is only a reference for
reports. If no connection is listed at all, your Qualtrics brand
administrator has to switch SSO on for survey authenticators.

## Questions and answers

### How do I ask that I want something else?
Ask directly opening an [issue](https://github.com/all-hands/survey-skill/issues). You can also contribute directly with a [pull request](https://github.com/all-hands/survey-skill/pulls).

### Participants pick 3 options and then rank them. Do they have to move anything, or can they just click Next?

With a drag-and-drop ranking and **Force response** on, an untouched
ranking counts as unanswered, so Next shows "Please answer this
question". Participants have to drag at least one item (they can drop it back
in place). Without Force response, an untouched ranking is saved as
blank, not as 1 to 3.

The easier option is to show the ranking as radio buttons: one row per
option, one column per rank, each rank used once. It is also easier to
use with a keyboard or screen reader.

### Can I make participants pick exactly 3 options, without JavaScript?

Yes. On the question, go to **Response requirements › Add validation ›
Answers range** and set both minimum and maximum to 3. Also turn on
**Force response**, so picking nothing doesn't pass. Test in preview with
0, 2, 3 and 4 options ticked.

"Minimum choices" on its own only checks the lower limit, so participants
could still pick 4 or more.

### How do I change the "Please answer this question." message?

Under **Survey options › Responses › Custom error messages**, create a
new message for "Require response", enter your text, save it and
publish. This changes the message for the whole survey, so keep the
wording general. For one question only, give that question its own
custom validation with its own message. You can change the text, not the
style.

### What else is worth setting before the survey goes live?

- Stop participants from taking the survey twice with the same login, or plan
  to keep only their newest response.
- Set a closing date.
- Write your own thank-you message for the end of the survey.
- Delete questions you no longer use, including those in the Trash
  block.
- Give questions readable export names (`preferred_session`, not `Q7`). That
  makes the results file much easier to work with.

## Emails after a response

### How do I email participants a copy of their answers?

With a workflow that sends an email after each response, with their
answers attached. The steps are in the guide:
[Email participants a copy of their answers](guide.md#email-participants-a-copy-of-their-answers).

### I set up a workflow that sends an email after each response, but nothing is sent. Why?

First open **Workflows › Run history**:

- **No run at all**: the trigger never fired.
- **Stopped at the condition**: the condition didn't match.
- **Email task failed**: the error is shown there.
- **Succeeded, but nothing arrived**: a delivery problem (spam folder,
  mail filters).

With sign-in surveys, the usual cause is the **To** field. "Recipient
Email" refers to a contact list, and is empty when participants sign in. Their
address comes from the sign-in as embedded data instead, so use the
`Email` embedded data field as the recipient. Also check that the
workflow is switched on and fires for new responses only. Unfinished
responses don't trigger it: the email goes out only after the last page.

## Look and feel

### I imported a sample and my organisation's logo appears. Is it in the file?

No. The samples don't name a theme, so Qualtrics uses your account's
default theme, which can include a logo. Change it per survey under
**Look & feel**.

### How do I make a theme the default?

Only a brand administrator can. In the admin pages, under **Themes**,
the theme at the top of the list becomes the default for new projects.
Existing surveys don't change. Everyone else can only pick a theme per
survey.

## For the technical colleague or AI assistant

### What surprised us in real `.qsf` exports?

- Messages (end of survey, error texts) are stored as references to the
  account's message library, so they break when the file is imported
  into another account. Set them again after import.
- A ranking fed by an earlier question keys its recodes as `x` plus the
  source choice ID.
- A copied survey's JavaScript can still contain the original survey's
  ID.
- A footer script can arrive cut off mid-code.
- A real export with sign-in contains the SSO connection's secret key.
  Treat it like a password and keep it out of the repo.

The skill (`skills/survey-qsf/SKILL.md`) covers these in detail.

---
name: survey-qsf
description: >-
  Quirks of Qualtrics .qsf survey files. Use when editing a real Qualtrics
  export, generating a .qsf to import, adding an SSO authenticator, branches,
  embedded data, carry-forward ranking, custom validation, JS or CSS, or when
  an import fails or SSO login breaks for some respondents.

# Qualtrics QSF: the quirks layer

You already know QSF basics (SurveyEntry, SurveyElements, BL/FL/SQ/SO, QIDs,
choices). This skill is the layer above: what real tenant exports actually
contain, what breaks silently, and how SSO behaves. Every quirk below was
observed in working exports, not inferred from docs, unless marked
*unverified*.

## 1. Pick the mode first

| Mode | When | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Fresh** | No export involved; you write the file | Portable defaults (§3), `validate_qsf.py --fresh` |
| **Edit in place** | User hands you a real export and wants a change | Keep every tenant field as found; recompute list (§4) |
| **Rebuild** | Export is broken beyond patching | Extract content, rebuild fresh, re-add tenant features from `references/feature-shapes.md` |

Mixing modes is the fatal habit: patching an export with fresh defaults
(blanket `SurveyBrandID: "qualtrics"`, stripping `PL`, renumbering QIDs)
destroys tenant configuration the user wanted kept. State the mode to the
user before the first write, and back the file up.

## 2. Export reality

Facts a genuine export holds that a hand-written file would not:

- **`BL.Payload` may be a keyed map**, `{"0": {...}, "1": {...}, "4": {...}}`,
  with gaps where blocks were deleted. The array form imports too. Edit in
  place: keep the form you found.
- **Block IDs are free-form**: readable IDs shaped like `BL_Intro01`
  occur in real exports. Read
  with `BL_[A-Za-z0-9]+`; mint `BL_` + 15 alphanumerics. `SV_`/`UR_`/`RS_`
  were always 15.
- **Trash** can hold questions (each keeps its full `SQ`), need not be the
  last block, and never appears in the flow. `QC.SecondaryAttribute` counts
  **all** SQ elements, trashed included.
- **Flow item `Type` follows `SubType`, not the block's `Type`**: a BL block
  with a `SubType` key (even `""`) appears in flow as `"Type": "Standard"`;
  without it, `"Type": "Block"`.
- **FlowIDs are creation-ordered**: a branch can contain lower FlowIDs than
  itself, deleted items leave holes, and `Properties.Count` = max numeric
  FlowID, holes included. Inserting: mint `FL_<Count+1>`, bump `Count`, never
  renumber.
- **One block can sit in several branches** (one shared form reached by an
  SSO route and a manual route). Only the branch that fires shows it.
- **`/` is serialized as `\/`** inside strings (`q:\/\/QID2\/SelectableChoice\/1`).
  Same value after `json.load`; plain `/` imports fine. Never treat the two
  spellings as different values.
- **Type discipline per key**: SO `BackButton`, `SaveAndContinue`,
  `BallotBoxStuffingPrevention`, `SecureResponseFiles`, `RecaptchaV3` are
  strings `"true"`/`"false"`; `ProtectSelectionIds`, `ConfirmStart`,
  `AutoConfirmStart`, `AutoCloseSurvey` are JSON booleans; `ForceResponse` is
  `"ON"`/`"OFF"`; `RightOperand`, `MinChoices`, recode values are strings.
  Copy the observed type, never normalize.
- **Placeholder text** (`"Click to write Choice 1"`) marks an untouched
  editor question: template debris, usually trashed.
- **`SecondaryAttribute` of an SQ** is a ~100-char plain-text echo of the
  question, ending in `...`. Cosmetic; keep it roughly in sync.
- **"Copy survey" provenance**: a copy keeps owner `UR_`, every `BL_` and
  `QID`; mints new `SV_`, `RS_`, `PreviewID`; appends " - Copy"; resets
  `SurveyStatus` to `Inactive`. Same lineage, not a new design.
- **IDs hard-coded inside JS do not follow a copy**: an exported copy still
  used a `sessionStorage` key naming the *original* survey's `SV_` ID. Grep
  `QuestionJS` and `SO.Footer` for `SV_` after copying.
- **`SO.Footer` arrived cut mid-script** (a few thousand chars, unclosed
  `<script>`, IIFE never closed) in one export. Cause unknown; the
  validator warns on it. Move long JS into `QuestionJS` instead.
- **Message-library references travel as IDs only**: `EOSMessage`,
  `ValidationMessage`, and custom validation `Message.messageID` name a
  message in the owner's library (`MS_…` + `UR_…` library). In another
  account they dangle. Fresh files: `SurveyTermination: "DefaultMessage"`,
  no `MS_` IDs, re-pick custom messages in the editor after import. Keep
  each message ID with its library ID as a pair.
- **`PL` (preview link)** sits after `FL` in exports. Edit in place: leave
  it. Fresh: omit it; Qualtrics mints one.

## 3. Fresh-file defaults

`SurveyBrandID: "qualtrics"`, `SkinLibrary: "qualtrics"`,
`Skin.brandingId: null`, `SurveyStatus: "Inactive"`, synthetic `UR_` used for
both owner and creator (the importer replaces it), no `PL`, no `MS_` IDs,
array-form `BL` with an empty Trash block last. Never invent a tenant brand,
skin ID, SSO connection ID or library ID.

## 4. Recompute list

After any edit, recompute each of these. Every one has broken an import or a
survey when left stale:

1. `QC.SecondaryAttribute`: string of the SQ count, trashed included.
2. `FL.Payload.Properties.Count`: max FlowID.
3. `NextChoiceId` / `NextAnswerId`: strictly greater than the max ID in use.
4. `ChoiceOrder`: it is **both filter and order**. IDs need not be
   contiguous or sorted (`[..."7", "12", "8"...]` happens); a choice absent
   from `ChoiceOrder` is not displayed.
5. Every `QIDn` reference: SQ envelope, `Payload.QuestionID`, BlockElements,
   logic (`QuestionID`, `QuestionIDFromLocator`, `ChoiceLocator`,
   `LeftOperand`), `DynamicChoices.Locator`, `${q://…}` pipes in text, JS and
   embedded-data values.
6. Carry-forward keys: `RecodeValues`/`VariableNaming` on a carried-forward
   question are keyed `x` + source choice ID (`"x3"`), not plain IDs.
7. Branch coverage: every choice of a routing question still has a branch.

**Done when** `python3 scripts/validate_qsf.py <file>` (add `--fresh` in
fresh mode) reports 0 errors and you have read every warning; in edit mode,
a diff against the backup shows only the intended change.

The validator (stdlib, in this skill's `scripts/`) checks 1–6 plus IDs,
element set, SurveyID consistency, orphaned questions, flow→trash refs, SO
boolean types, dangling library pairs, footer scripts and SSO placement.
Branch coverage (7) is yours to check.

## 5. SSO in one screen

- Everything the respondent should answer **only after login** goes
  **inside** the authenticator's `Flow`. `respondentMap` writes IdP
  attributes into embedded data (`FirstName`, `LastName`, `Email`, an ID).
- **Put a welcome block before the authenticator.** Authenticator-first
  redirects to the IdP before any Qualtrics page renders; that layout failed
  for some respondents, while intro-then-authenticator worked.
- A failed login **skips the whole authenticated section**: respondent lands
  on the thank-you page, and an almost-empty response is recorded.
- SSO through `/jfe/preview/` links is unreliable by Qualtrics' own docs:
  test with the live anonymous link in a normal browser window.
- `SSOOptions.SSOID` and `token.Key` belong to a brand's SSO connection.
  Exports embed the key: **treat any export with an authenticator as a
  secret**. Samples here carry `X` placeholders; after import, open Survey
  flow → authenticator and pick your connection. The editor may *display*
  a connection while the flow still stores the placeholder; respondents
  then get "Error while determining which SSO connection to use for this
  survey". Fix: switch SSO Type to another value, save, switch back,
  re-select the connection, save, publish.
- `allowRetake: true` means one person can produce several rows: dedupe on
  the ID field, last submission wins.

Read `references/sso.md` when wiring a new authenticator, mixing SSO with a
non-SSO route, or diagnosing "SSO works for me, not for them".

## 6. Feature shapes

`references/feature-shapes.md` holds copy-ready JSON, from working exports,
for: embedded data (declare, then set per branch), branches with
descriptions, select-exactly-N with custom validation, multi-column
multi-select, drag-and-drop ranking with carry-forward, display logic,
perma-hide, matrix grid, email validation, QuestionJS/CSS, and recodes.
Read it before adding any of those to a file.

## 7. Samples

Three importable, anonymized samples in `samples/`. Each has an SSO
authenticator, never as the first flow element: a welcome page (or, in the
event sample, event details plus a route question) comes first. The event
sample also offers a manual route around SSO. Pick the nearest, copy it,
change text, keep the shapes.

| File | Shows |
|---|---|
| `session-availability-sso.qsf` | Welcome → authenticator → identity card (`${e://Field/…}` piping) + matrix grid (session × attendance mode) with `VariableNaming` |
| `ranked-preferences-sso.qsf` | Opt-in branch with embedded data per route; pick exactly 3 of 10 (custom validation + JS limiter, 2 columns); drag-rank the picks (carry-forward, `x`-keyed recodes); `SubType: ""` block spelled `Standard` in flow |
| `event-attendance-sso.qsf` | SSO route **or** manual route into one shared block; display logic per route; manual answers copied into the same embedded fields; RSVP yes/no recoded `1`/`0` and mirrored to `RsvpStatus`; static Outlook/Google calendar links plus an `.ics` download built as a blob URL in `QuestionJS` |

Import: new project → Survey → *Import a QSF file*. Then: set the SSO
connection in Survey flow, publish, test on the anonymous link. The samples
are structurally validated, not import-tested in every account; *unverified*:
whether a custom validation `Message` without library IDs keeps its
description text on import.

## 8. Postflight

- [ ] Mode stated; backup taken (edit mode)
- [ ] Recompute list done; validator 0 errors, warnings read
- [ ] No tenant field baseline-ified (edit) / no tenant field invented (fresh)
- [ ] Authenticator after a welcome block; SSO placeholders or real values handled per §5
- [ ] File with a real SSO key kept out of public repos, chats and open shares
- [ ] Hand-off reminder (§9) in your reply

## 9. Hand-off reminder

Whenever your reply delivers or changes a `.qsf` that contains an
authenticator, end the reply with this reminder, adapted to the user's
SSO type:

> **After import, register the SSO connection, or respondents get "Error
> while determining which SSO connection to use for this survey":**
> 1. Survey flow → click the authenticator.
> 2. SSO Type: select another type, save the flow.
> 3. SSO Type: back to Shibboleth (or your type), select your connection,
>    save the flow.
> 4. Publish. If saving does not stick, publish and unpublish, then
>    publish again.
> 5. Test with the anonymous link in a normal browser window, not preview.

The editor shows a connection even when the flow still stores a
placeholder or another brand's `SSOID`; only the switch-and-save makes it
stick. Confirmed on a sample import.

===============================================================================
FILE: skills/survey-qsf/references/sso.md
===============================================================================
# SSO authenticator: shape, placement, failure modes

Reached from `SKILL.md` §5. Observed on two surveys using the same
Shibboleth connection with an identical authenticator config: one worked
for every respondent tested, the other failed for some.

## Shape (Shibboleth)

"Shibboleth" is Qualtrics' label for SAML-based SSO ("Respondents
authenticate via SAML"), whatever SAML identity provider the organisation
runs. Other SSO types: Token, CAS, LDAP, Google OAuth 2.0, Facebook.

```json
{
  "Type": "Authenticator",
  "FlowID": "FL_3",
  "FilterDataFields": true,
  "SSOOptions": {
    "respondentMap": [
      { "key": "urn:oid:2.5.4.42",                  "value": "FirstName" },
      { "key": "urn:oid:2.5.4.4",                   "value": "LastName" },
      { "key": "urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3", "value": "Email" },
      { "key": "urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.1", "value": "UserID" }
    ],
    "Type": "Shibboleth",
    "token": { "EncryptionMethod": "3DES", "MacMethod": "sha512",
               "Leeway": 300, "Key": "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX" },
    "ldap": { "Hostname": "ldap://", "Port": "389", "EmailField": "mail",
              "Filter": "(sAMAccountName=%1)", "FirstNameField": "givenname",
              "LastNameField": "sn", "ExternalDataReferenceField": "" },
    "UsePanel": "No", "CaptureRespondentInfo": "Yes", "UseSSO": "Yes",
    "SSOID": "ASC_XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX", "cas": []
  },
  "Options": {
    "maxAttempts": 3,
    "questionText":              { "SystemMessage": { "Section": "ErrorCodes", "Message": "EAUTH04" } },
    "authenticationError":       { "SystemMessage": { "Section": "ErrorCodes", "Message": "EAUTH02" } },
    "failedAuthenticationError": { "SystemMessage": { "Section": "ErrorCodes", "Message": "EAUTH05" } },
    "allowRetake": true, "loadExistingSession": false, "reauthenticateSession": false
  },
  "Flow": [ "...everything that needs a signed-in respondent..." ]
}
```

- `respondentMap` keys are SAML attribute OIDs (givenName, sn, mail, uid);
  values are embedded-data field names, which become response columns. The
  IdP decides which attributes it releases; a missing one arrives blank.
- `token` and `ldap` are carried even for Shibboleth (default-looking
  values). `token.Key` is real secret material in an export.
- `SSOID` (`ASC_…`) names the brand-level SSO connection. It is per brand:
  a file moved to another brand needs the connection re-picked in Survey
  flow. Wrong or disabled connection shows Qualtrics error
  `AUTHENTICATOR_SSO_CONFIG_DISABLED` / `…_NOT_FOUND` for **everyone**.
- `Autofill` is never on an authenticator item; only on Block/Standard.

## Placement

| Layout | Observed |
|---|---|
| Authenticator as very first flow element, all blocks inside | Worked for some respondents, failed for others |
| Welcome page first, authenticator inside a branch after a routing question | Worked for everyone tested |

Authenticator-first redirects to the IdP on the first page load, before any
Qualtrics page has set its session; embedded/in-app browsers and strict
cookie settings are likelier to lose the session on that immediate
redirect. Qualtrics' own advice is "move the authenticator to the beginning
of your survey flow", so authenticator-first is not a config *error*, just
the riskier layout. Default: a welcome block with **no** `${e://Field/…}`
piping (nothing is filled before login), then the authenticator.

## What failure looks like

- Login fails → after `maxAttempts`, Qualtrics **skips the authenticated
  section**. If every block is inside it, the respondent goes straight to
  the thank-you page. "SSO broken" is reported as "the survey ends at once".
- Failed authentications **are recorded as responses**: rows with no
  identity fields. Filter rows without the ID/email before analysis.
- Login works, attributes missing → identity card shows blank name/email.
  IdP attribute release for that account type; the IdP admins fix it.

## Diagnosis: "works for me, not for them"

Identical config cannot fail for one person only, so look at how they open
it:

| Symptom | Likely cause | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Never reaches the IdP login | Preview link, or browser | URL contains `/jfe/preview/` → send the live anonymous link `/jfe/form/SV_…` |
| Bounces between IdP and Qualtrics | Cookies lost across the redirect | Opened inside Teams/Outlook/mail app, private mode, strict tracking protection, ad-block → normal Chrome/Edge window, extensions off |
| IdP shows "not authorised for this service" | Account type not released to Qualtrics | Guest/external/staff vs regular account → IdP admins |
| Lands on thank-you page immediately | Login failed and was skipped | Combine with the rows above; look for an empty response at that time |
| Identity card blank | Attributes not released | IdP admins |
| "Error while determining which SSO connection to use for this survey. Please contact your brand administrator." plus a report tag | Imported file's `SSOID` is unknown in this brand (placeholder or another brand's ID). The editor *displays* a connection but has not stored it | Survey flow → authenticator: switch SSO Type to another value, save; switch back, re-select the connection, save, publish. If saving does not stick, publish/unpublish to force it. Confirmed fix on a sample import |
| Silent login as the wrong person | Already signed in to the IdP with another account | Sign out of the IdP or use a fresh browser profile |

Cross-check: have them open a survey whose SSO is known to work, in the
same browser. Fails there too → their account or browser. Works there →
try the welcome-block-first layout.

## Mixed SSO and non-SSO routes

To admit participants without an account while keeping one response schema:

1. Default block: welcome + routing question ("Sign in" / "Register without
   signing in").
2. Branch on choice 1 → authenticator → embedded `LoginMethod = SSO` →
   shared form block.
3. Branch on choice 2 → embedded `LoginMethod = Manual` and declare
   `FirstName`/`LastName`/`Email`/ID empty → same shared form block →
   embedded data copying `${q://QIDn/ChoiceTextEntryValue}` of the typed
   name/email into the same fields.
4. In the shared block, display logic per route: identity card (piped) for
   SSO, text-entry name/email (required, email `ContentType: ValidEmail`)
   for manual. Hidden required questions do not block the page.

Every row then has the same identity columns regardless of route; typed
addresses are less reliable than SSO ones (expect bounces).

## Other options

- `maxAttempts`: Qualtrics generally advises against it for SSO; it matters
  only with "associate respondent with panel" (`UsePanel: "Yes"`). Observed
  value 3 is harmless.
- `allowRetake: true` → repeat submissions; decide a rule (last per ID
  wins) or turn it off.
- `loadExistingSession` / `reauthenticateSession`: reload saved progress /
  force re-login on resume. Both `false` in every observed survey.
- Bot detection (`RecaptchaV3`) only adds a score; it never blocks
  respondents, so it is not an SSO suspect.

## Sources

- Qualtrics, [SSO Authenticator](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/sso-authenticator/): Shibboleth section, preview limitation ("may not function properly with preview survey"), test via anonymous link, error codes, max-attempts advice.
- Qualtrics, [Authenticator Overview](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-flow/advanced-elements/authenticator/authenticator-overview/): placement, retake/reload options, failed authentications recorded as responses, skip-past behaviour.
- Qualtrics, [Fraud Detection](https://www.qualtrics.com/support/survey-platform/survey-module/survey-checker/fraud-detection/): bot detection never blocks respondents.

===============================================================================
FILE: skills/survey-qsf/references/feature-shapes.md
===============================================================================
# Feature shapes

Copy-ready shapes from working exports, reached from `SKILL.md` §6. QIDs and
FlowIDs are examples: renumber to your file and run the recompute list
afterwards. Each shape is used in at least one file in `../samples/`.

## Embedded data: declare, then set per branch

Declare once (empty `Value`) before branching, set inside each branch.
`Value` takes a literal or a pipe.

```json
{ "Type": "EmbeddedData", "FlowID": "FL_4",
  "EmbeddedData": [
    { "Description": "OptIn", "Type": "Custom", "Field": "OptIn",
      "VariableType": "Nominal", "DataVisibility": [], "Value": "" } ],
  "Options": { "VarTypes": "Yes" } }
```

```json
{ "Type": "Custom", "Description": "Email", "Field": "Email",
  "Value": "${q://QID6/ChoiceTextEntryValue}", "VariableType": "Nominal" }
```

`DataVisibility: []` appears on some field rows and not others in exports;
both import. Flow items of type EmbeddedData, Branch and Authenticator carry
no `Autofill`; Block/Standard items carry `"Autofill": []`.

Use embedded fields as the **stable contract** for downstream code (exports,
mail merges): set a route or status field per branch instead of making
scripts decode choice IDs.

## Branch

```json
{ "Type": "Branch", "FlowID": "FL_6", "Description": "Yes — choose 3, rank, comment",
  "BranchLogic": { "0": { "0": {
      "LogicType": "Question", "QuestionID": "QID3", "QuestionIsInLoop": "no",
      "ChoiceLocator": "q://QID3/SelectableChoice/1", "Operator": "Selected",
      "QuestionIDFromLocator": "QID3", "LeftOperand": "q://QID3/SelectableChoice/1",
      "Type": "Expression", "Description": "If QID3 choice 1 is selected" },
    "Type": "If" }, "Type": "BooleanExpression" },
  "Flow": [ ... ] }
```

`Description` is the label in the flow editor and survives export: write
route names. A second condition in the same group is key `"1"` with
`"Conjuction": "Or"` (Qualtrics' spelling, one *n*).

## Display logic on a question

Same expression object, wrapped with `inPage`:

```json
"DisplayLogic": { "0": { "0": {
    "ChoiceLocator": "q://QID2/SelectableChoice/2",
    "Description": "<span class=\"ConjDesc\">If</span> <span class=\"QuestionDesc\">How would you like to register?</span> <span class=\"LeftOpDesc\">Register without signing in</span> <span class=\"OpDesc\">Is Selected</span> ",
    "LeftOperand": "q://QID2/SelectableChoice/2", "LogicType": "Question",
    "Operator": "Selected", "QuestionID": "QID2", "QuestionIDFromLocator": "QID2",
    "QuestionIsInLoop": "no", "Type": "Expression" },
  "Type": "If" }, "Type": "BooleanExpression", "inPage": false }
```

`Description` is HTML the editor renders; exports may hold stray newlines
inside it. Content is cosmetic, the locators are what run.

## Perma-hide (park a question without trashing it)

```json
"DisplayLogic": { "0": { "0": {
    "LogicType": "BooleanValue", "Value": "False", "Type": "Expression",
    "Description": "<span class=\"ConjDesc\">If</span><span> False</span>" },
  "Type": "If" }, "Type": "BooleanExpression", "inPage": false }
```

The other way: move its BlockElements entry into the Trash block and keep
its SQ.

## Select exactly N (custom validation)

```json
"Validation": { "Settings": {
  "ForceResponse": "OFF", "ForceResponseType": "ON", "Type": "CustomValidation",
  "MinChoices": "3", "MaxChoices": "3",
  "CustomValidation": {
    "Logic": { "0": { "0": {
        "ChoiceLocator": "q://QID4/SelectedChoicesCount",
        "LeftOperand": "q://QID4/SelectedChoicesCount",
        "Operator": "EqualTo", "RightOperand": "3",
        "LogicType": "Question", "QuestionID": "QID4", "QuestionIDFromLocator": "QID4",
        "QuestionIsInLoop": "no", "Type": "Expression", "Description": "..." },
      "Type": "If" }, "Type": "BooleanExpression" },
    "Message": { "description": "Please select exactly 3 options.",
                 "subMessageID": "VE_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_0" } } } }
```

`ForceResponse: "OFF"` with the custom validation doing the enforcing is
normal. In exports `Message` also carries `messageID` + `libraryID` (owner's
library); drop both in fresh files. Pair with a JS limiter that disables
further boxes at N (see `ranked-preferences-sso.qsf`, QID4) so the error
rarely fires.

Exports also use `CustomValidation` as a disguised force-response (OR of
"choice 1 selected", "choice 2 selected", `subMessageID:
"VE_FORCE_RESPONSE"`). Plain `"ForceResponse": "ON"` does the same job.

## Multi-select in columns

```json
"QuestionType": "MC", "Selector": "MACOL", "SubSelector": "TX",
"Configuration": { "QuestionDescriptionOption": "UseText", "NumColumns": 2 }
```

Column count lives in `Configuration`, not in the choices.

## Drag-and-drop ranking of carried-forward choices

```json
{ "QuestionType": "RO", "Selector": "DND", "SubSelector": "TX",
  "Choices": [], "ChoiceOrder": [], "NextChoiceId": 1,
  "DynamicChoices": { "DynamicType": "ChoiceGroup",
                      "Locator": "q://QID4/ChoiceGroup/SelectedChoices", "Type": "Dynamic" },
  "DynamicChoicesData": [],
  "Validation": { "Settings": { "ForceResponse": "ON", "ForceResponseType": "ON", "Type": "None" } },
  "RecodeValues":   { "x1": "1", "x2": "2" },
  "VariableNaming": { "x1": "P01 — Customer onboarding redesign", "x2": "P02 — ..." } }
```

- `Choices` is an **empty array**, not `{}`.
- Carried-forward choices are keyed **`x` + source choice ID**. Keys without
  the `x` match nothing.
- The source question must show earlier in flow order.
- With `ForceResponse: "ON"`, a respondent who likes the default order must
  still drag one item (anywhere, even back in place) before the page
  submits. Say so in the question text.
- Piping `${q://QID4/ChoiceGroup/SelectedChoices}` on a review page shows the
  picks in **choice order, not rank order**. One export had such a review
  page, parked in Trash.

## Matrix grid (one answer per row)

```json
{ "QuestionType": "Matrix", "Selector": "Likert", "SubSelector": "SingleAnswer",
  "Configuration": { "QuestionDescriptionOption": "UseText", "TextPosition": "inline",
                     "ChoiceColumnWidth": 45, "RepeatHeaders": "none",
                     "WhiteSpace": "OFF", "MobileFirst": true },
  "Choices": { "1": { "Display": "Monday 1 March 2027, 09:00-11:00" } },
  "ChoiceOrder": ["1"],
  "Answers": { "1": { "Display": "No" }, "2": { "Display": "Remote" } },
  "AnswerOrder": ["1", "2"],
  "RecodeValues":   { "1": "1", "2": "2" },
  "VariableNaming": { "1": "NO", "2": "REMOTE" },
  "NextChoiceId": 2, "NextAnswerId": 3,
  "DefaultChoices": false, "ChoiceDataExportTags": false, "GradingData": [] }
```

Rows are `Choices`, columns are `Answers`; on a matrix, `RecodeValues` and
`VariableNaming` key on **answers**. Both `Next…Id` counters apply.

## Text entry

```json
"QuestionType": "TE", "Selector": "SL",
"Validation": { "Settings": { "ForceResponse": "ON", "ForceResponseType": "ON",
                              "Type": "ContentType", "ContentType": "ValidEmail" } },
"SearchSource": { "AllowFreeResponse": "false" }
```

`Selector` `SL` single line, `ML` multi-line (box size in
`Configuration.InputWidth`/`InputHeight`). `SearchSource` rides along on TE
exports.

## Recodes and labels

- `RecodeValues` may be non-monotonic: yes/no as `{"1": "1",
  "2": "0"}` makes the column a 0/1 flag.
- `VariableNaming` gives choices short analysis labels (`"1": "P01"`).
- Both are string→string maps at payload level.
- `DataExportTag` is the response column name: make it semantic
  (`rsvp`) and treat it as contract between survey waves.

## Custom code

- `QuestionJS`: one string of JS using
  `Qualtrics.SurveyEngine.addOnReady` / `addOnPageSubmit`; several hooks
  may sit in one string. Observed uses: change the Next button label,
  limit checkbox count, build an `.ics` blob URL, write to `sessionStorage`.
- `SO.CustomStyles.customCSS`: raw CSS for the whole survey. `:has()` works
  for styling selected choices.
- `SO.Footer`: HTML including `<script>`; see the truncation quirk in
  `SKILL.md` §2. Prefer `QuestionJS`.
- Inline-styled HTML in `QuestionText` (cards, buttons) survives round
  trips. Edit in place: preserve all of the above byte for byte.

===============================================================================
FILE: skills/survey-qsf/scripts/validate_qsf.py
===============================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Structural validator for Qualtrics .qsf files.

Default mode accepts genuine tenant exports (keyed-map BL, free-form block
IDs, FlowID gaps, trashed questions). --fresh adds the rules for files you
generate yourself (array BL, 15-char IDs, neutral brand, no PL, no
message-library refs).

    python3 validate_qsf.py survey.qsf [more.qsf ...] [--fresh]

Prints ERROR / WARN lines; exit 1 if any ERROR.
Stdlib only.
"""
import json
import re
import sys

ID15 = r"[A-Za-z0-9]{15}"
STRING_BOOL_SO_KEYS = ("BackButton", "SaveAndContinue", "BallotBoxStuffingPrevention", "SecureResponseFiles",
                       "RecaptchaV3")
REAL_BOOL_SO_KEYS = ("ProtectSelectionIds", "ConfirmStart", "AutoConfirmStart", "AutoCloseSurvey")
MESSAGE_PAIRS = (("EOSMessage", "EOSMessageLibrary"), ("InactiveMessage", "InactiveMessageLibrary"),
                 ("ThankYouEmailMessage", "ThankYouEmailMessageLibrary"),
                 ("ValidationMessage", "ValidationMessageLibrary"))
PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"^(ASC_)?X+$")


class Report:
    def __init__(self):
        self.errors, self.warnings = [], []

    def error(self, msg):
        self.errors.append(msg)

    def warn(self, msg):
        self.warnings.append(msg)


def walk_strings(node, path=""):
    """Yield (path, string) for every string value in a JSON tree."""
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        for k, v in node.items():
            yield from walk_strings(v, f"{path}.{k}")
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for i, v in enumerate(node):
            yield from walk_strings(v, f"{path}[{i}]")
    elif isinstance(node, str):
        yield path, node


def walk_flow(item, depth=0, inside_auth=False):
    """Yield (flow_item, depth, inside_authenticator) depth-first, in display order."""
    yield item, depth, inside_auth
    child_auth = inside_auth or item.get("Type") == "Authenticator"
    for child in item.get("Flow", []) or []:
        yield from walk_flow(child, depth + 1, child_auth)


def blocks_of(bl_payload, rep, fresh):
    if isinstance(bl_payload, list):
        return list(bl_payload)
    if isinstance(bl_payload, dict):
        if fresh:
            rep.error("BL.Payload is a keyed map; generate the array form for fresh files")
        return [bl_payload[k] for k in sorted(bl_payload, key=lambda k: int(k) if k.isdigit() else 0)]
    rep.error("BL.Payload is neither an array nor a keyed map")
    return []


def choice_keys(payload):
    choices = payload.get("Choices")
    if isinstance(choices, dict):
        return set(choices)
    return set()


def max_int(keys):
    nums = [int(k) for k in keys if str(k).isdigit()]
    return max(nums) if nums else 0


def validate(doc, fresh=False):
    rep = Report()
    if not isinstance(doc, dict) or "SurveyEntry" not in doc or "SurveyElements" not in doc:
        rep.error("top level must hold SurveyEntry and SurveyElements")
        return rep
    entry, elements = doc["SurveyEntry"], doc["SurveyElements"]

    # --- SurveyEntry -----------------------------------------------------
    sv = entry.get("SurveyID", "")
    if not re.fullmatch(f"SV_{ID15}", sv or ""):
        rep.error(f"SurveyEntry.SurveyID {sv!r} is not SV_ + 15 alphanumerics")
    for key in ("SurveyOwnerID", "CreatorID"):
        if not re.fullmatch(f"UR_{ID15}", entry.get(key) or ""):
            rep.error(f"SurveyEntry.{key} must be UR_ + 15 alphanumerics, never blank")
    if fresh and entry.get("SurveyBrandID") != "qualtrics":
        rep.error("fresh file: SurveyBrandID should be the neutral 'qualtrics'")

    by_type = {}
    for el in elements:
        by_type.setdefault(el.get("Element"), []).append(el)
        if el.get("SurveyID") != sv:
            rep.error(f"element {el.get('Element')} {el.get('PrimaryAttribute')} carries SurveyID "
                      f"{el.get('SurveyID')!r}, expected {sv!r}")
    for need in ("BL", "FL", "QC", "RS", "SO", "STAT"):
        if len(by_type.get(need, [])) != 1:
            rep.error(f"need exactly one {need} element, found {len(by_type.get(need, []))}")
    for soft in ("PROJ", "SCO"):
        if soft not in by_type:
            rep.warn(f"no {soft} element (real exports always carry one)")
    if fresh and "PL" in by_type:
        rep.error("fresh file: omit PL; Qualtrics mints the preview link on import")
    if rep.errors:
        return rep

    rs = by_type["RS"][0]
    if entry.get("SurveyActiveResponseSet") != rs.get("PrimaryAttribute"):
        rep.error("SurveyActiveResponseSet does not match the RS element's PrimaryAttribute")

    # --- SQ ----------------------------------------------------------------
    questions = {}
    tags = {}
    for el in by_type.get("SQ", []):
        p = el.get("Payload") or {}
        qid = el.get("PrimaryAttribute")
        if qid in questions:
            rep.error(f"duplicate SQ {qid}")
        if p.get("QuestionID") != qid:
            rep.error(f"SQ {qid}: Payload.QuestionID is {p.get('QuestionID')!r}")
        questions[qid] = p
        tag = p.get("DataExportTag")
        if tag in tags:
            rep.warn(f"DataExportTag {tag!r} used by {tags[tag]} and {qid}")
        tags[tag] = qid

    qc = by_type["QC"][0].get("SecondaryAttribute")
    if qc != str(len(questions)):
        rep.error(f"QC.SecondaryAttribute is {qc!r}; SQ count (trashed included) is {len(questions)}")

    # --- BL ----------------------------------------------------------------
    blocks = blocks_of(by_type["BL"][0].get("Payload"), rep, fresh)
    block_ids, trash_ids = {}, set()
    placed = {}
    defaults = 0
    for b in blocks:
        bid = b.get("ID", "")
        pattern = f"BL_{ID15}" if fresh else r"BL_[A-Za-z0-9]+"
        if not re.fullmatch(pattern, bid):
            rep.error(f"block ID {bid!r} does not match {pattern}")
        if bid in block_ids:
            rep.error(f"duplicate block ID {bid}")
        block_ids[bid] = b
        if b.get("Type") == "Trash":
            trash_ids.add(bid)
        if b.get("Type") == "Default":
            defaults += 1
        for be in b.get("BlockElements", []) or []:
            if be.get("Type") != "Question":
                continue
            q = be.get("QuestionID")
            if q not in questions:
                rep.error(f"block {bid} references missing question {q}")
            if q in placed:
                rep.error(f"{q} sits in two blocks ({placed[q]} and {bid})")
            placed[q] = bid
    if defaults != 1:
        rep.warn(f"expected one Default block, found {defaults}")
    if len(trash_ids) > 1:
        rep.error("more than one Trash block")
    for q in questions:
        if q not in placed:
            rep.error(f"{q} is orphaned: in no block (not even Trash)")

    # --- FL ----------------------------------------------------------------
    root = by_type["FL"][0].get("Payload") or {}
    if root.get("Type") != "Root" or root.get("FlowID") != "FL_1":
        rep.error("FL root must be Type Root with FlowID FL_1")
    seen_fids = {}
    flow_blocks = []
    auth_items = []
    for item, depth, inside_auth in walk_flow(root):
        fid = item.get("FlowID", "")
        if not re.fullmatch(r"FL_\d+", fid):
            rep.error(f"bad FlowID {fid!r}")
            continue
        if fid in seen_fids:
            rep.error(f"duplicate FlowID {fid}")
        seen_fids[fid] = item
        t = item.get("Type")
        if t in ("Block", "Standard"):
            bid = item.get("ID")
            flow_blocks.append(bid)
            if bid not in block_ids:
                rep.error(f"flow {fid} points at missing block {bid}")
            elif bid in trash_ids:
                rep.error(f"flow {fid} points at the Trash block")
            else:
                want = "Standard" if "SubType" in block_ids[bid] else "Block"
                if t != want:
                    rep.warn(f"flow {fid} is Type {t!r}; block {bid} "
                             f"{'has' if want == 'Standard' else 'lacks'} SubType, exports spell it {want!r}")
        if t == "Authenticator":
            auth_items.append((item, depth))
    if root.get("Type") == "Root":
        count = (root.get("Properties") or {}).get("Count")
        top = max(int(f[3:]) for f in seen_fids) if seen_fids else 0
        if count != top:
            rep.error(f"FL Properties.Count is {count!r}; max FlowID is {top}")
    for bid in block_ids:
        if bid not in trash_ids and bid not in flow_blocks:
            rep.warn(f"block {bid} ({block_ids[bid].get('Description')!r}) is not in the flow; "
                     "its questions never show")

    # question display order, for carry-forward checks
    order = []
    for bid in flow_blocks:
        for be in (block_ids.get(bid) or {}).get("BlockElements", []) or []:
            if be.get("QuestionID") not in order:
                order.append(be.get("QuestionID"))

    # --- per-question payload checks ---------------------------------------
    for qid, p in questions.items():
        keys = choice_keys(p)
        dyn = p.get("DynamicChoices")
        co = p.get("ChoiceOrder")
        if isinstance(co, list):
            stray = [str(c) for c in co if str(c) not in keys]
            if stray and not dyn:
                rep.error(f"{qid}: ChoiceOrder lists unknown choice IDs {stray}")
        nci = p.get("NextChoiceId")
        if keys and isinstance(nci, int) and nci <= max_int(keys):
            rep.error(f"{qid}: NextChoiceId {nci} must exceed max choice ID {max_int(keys)}")
        answers = p.get("Answers")
        if isinstance(answers, dict):
            nai = p.get("NextAnswerId")
            if isinstance(nai, int) and nai <= max_int(answers):
                rep.error(f"{qid}: NextAnswerId {nai} must exceed max answer ID {max_int(answers)}")
            ao = p.get("AnswerOrder") or []
            stray = [str(a) for a in ao if str(a) not in answers]
            if stray:
                rep.error(f"{qid}: AnswerOrder lists unknown answer IDs {stray}")
        if dyn:
            m = re.match(r"q://(QID\d+)/", dyn.get("Locator", ""))
            src = m.group(1) if m else None
            if src not in questions:
                rep.error(f"{qid}: DynamicChoices source {src!r} does not exist")
            else:
                if src in order and qid in order and order.index(src) > order.index(qid):
                    rep.error(f"{qid}: carry-forward source {src} shows after it")
                src_keys = {f"x{k}" for k in choice_keys(questions[src])}
                for field in ("RecodeValues", "VariableNaming"):
                    extra = set(p.get(field) or {}) - src_keys
                    if extra:
                        rep.error(f"{qid}: {field} keys {sorted(extra)} are not x + a {src} choice ID")
        else:
            labels = keys if p.get("QuestionType") != "Matrix" else set(answers or {})
            for field in ("RecodeValues", "VariableNaming"):
                extra = set(p.get(field) or {}) - labels
                if extra and labels:
                    rep.error(f"{qid}: {field} keys {sorted(extra)} match no choice/answer")
        fr = ((p.get("Validation") or {}).get("Settings") or {}).get("ForceResponse")
        if fr is not None and fr not in ("ON", "OFF"):
            rep.error(f"{qid}: ForceResponse must be the string 'ON' or 'OFF'")
        if fresh and "QuestionJS" in p and not p["QuestionJS"].lstrip().startswith("Qualtrics.SurveyEngine"):
            rep.warn(f"{qid}: QuestionJS does not start with a Qualtrics.SurveyEngine hook")

    # --- references anywhere in the file -----------------------------------
    for path, s in walk_strings(doc):
        for qid, rest in re.findall(r"q:(?:\\?/){2}(QID\d+)((?:\\?/)[A-Za-z]+(?:\\?/)?\d*)?", s):
            if qid not in questions:
                rep.error(f"{path}: reference to missing {qid}")
                continue
            m = re.search(r"SelectableChoice(?:\\?/)(\d+)", rest or "")
            if m and questions[qid].get("Choices") and m.group(1) not in choice_keys(questions[qid]):
                rep.error(f"{path}: {qid} has no choice {m.group(1)}")
        if fresh and re.search(r"\bMS_[A-Za-z0-9]{15}\b", s):
            rep.error(f"{path}: message-library ID in a fresh file; it will dangle in another account")

    # --- SO ----------------------------------------------------------------
    so = by_type["SO"][0].get("Payload") or {}
    for key in STRING_BOOL_SO_KEYS:
        if key in so and not isinstance(so[key], str):
            rep.error(f"SO.{key} must be a string ('true'/'false'), got {type(so[key]).__name__}")
    for key in REAL_BOOL_SO_KEYS:
        if key in so and not isinstance(so[key], bool):
            rep.error(f"SO.{key} must be a JSON boolean, got {type(so[key]).__name__}")
    for msg, lib in MESSAGE_PAIRS:
        if so.get(msg) and str(so[msg]).startswith("MS_") and not so.get(lib):
            rep.error(f"SO.{msg} names a library message but SO.{lib} is empty")
    footer = so.get("Footer") or ""
    if footer.count("<script") > footer.count("</script>"):
        rep.warn(f"SO.Footer has an unclosed <script> ({len(footer)} chars); exports have been seen "
                 "cut mid-script, so check it on the live survey")
    if fresh:
        skin = so.get("Skin") or {}
        if so.get("SkinLibrary") != "qualtrics" or skin.get("brandingId") is not None:
            rep.error("fresh file: use SkinLibrary 'qualtrics' and Skin.brandingId null")

    # --- SSO authenticators ------------------------------------------------
    first = (root.get("Flow") or [{}])[0] if root.get("Flow") else {}
    for item, depth in auth_items:
        sso = item.get("SSOOptions") or {}
        fid = item.get("FlowID")
        if PLACEHOLDER.match(sso.get("SSOID") or ""):
            rep.warn(f"{fid}: SSOID is a placeholder; after import, Survey flow -> authenticator: switch SSO Type "
                     "to another value, save, switch back, select your connection, save, publish")
        key = (sso.get("token") or {}).get("Key")
        if key and not PLACEHOLDER.match(key):
            rep.warn(f"{fid}: SSO token key present; treat this file as a secret")
        if item is first:
            rep.warn(f"{fid}: authenticator is the very first flow element; respondents bounce to the IdP "
                     "before any page renders (fragile in in-app browsers). Put a welcome block first")
        if not item.get("Flow"):
            rep.error(f"{fid}: authenticator has an empty Flow; nothing is protected")
    return rep


def main(argv):
    fresh = "--fresh" in argv
    files = [a for a in argv if a != "--fresh"]
    if not files:
        print(__doc__.strip())
        return 2
    failed = False
    for path in files:
        try:
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                doc = json.load(fh)
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            print(f"{path}: ERROR cannot load JSON: {exc}")
            failed = True
            continue
        rep = validate(doc, fresh=fresh)
        for e in rep.errors:
            print(f"{path}: ERROR {e}")
        for w in rep.warnings:
            print(f"{path}: WARN {w}")
        print(f"{path}: {'FAIL' if rep.errors else 'OK'} ({len(rep.errors)} errors, {len(rep.warnings)} warnings)")
        failed = failed or bool(rep.errors)
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

===============================================================================
